title: Excise harness shape profile v1
description: The shape of one tree, as aggregates only: counts of entries by kind and by depth, what a folder holds and how large a file is in classes of powers of two, the lengths of names in bytes, and the share of hard links and symbolic links. It never holds a name, a path, a link target, an owner, or a timestamp. Internal test tooling, not a supported product interface. Written by excise-shape profile; excise-shape spec builds a fixture specification from one. A profile can come from anywhere, so a reader holds it to this schema, and to the rules in the harness README that a schema cannot say, before it uses a field.

max_depth.description: The deepest depth that holds an entry, 0 for an empty tree. It equals the length of depths.

depths.description: The entries and bytes at each depth from 1 to max_depth, in order. Depth 1 is what the root directly holds.

children_per_directory.description: The entries a folder holds, of every kind, for each folder that was listed (the root included).

subdirectories_per_directory.description: The folders a folder holds, for each folder that was listed.

files_per_directory.description: The regular files a folder holds, for each folder that was listed.

file_sizes.description: The apparent size (st_size) of each regular file, every name of a hard-linked file counted. Its total is the bytes of the tree.

count.description: A non-negative whole number that every JSON consumer reads back exactly (at most 2^53 - 1).

positive_count.description: A count of at least 1: a bucket that holds nothing is left out.

unsigned.description: A non-negative whole number that fits 64 bits. A sum of sizes and a largest size can pass 2^53, which a sparse file makes possible, and a JSON consumer other than a 64-bit reader may then round it.

os.description: The operating system as std::env::consts::OS spells it, for example macos.

identity.description: Whether the platform reported a device and an inode for every entry. Without them (Windows) the walk finds no mount point and no hard link.

cross_filesystems.description: Whether the walk was asked to cross into other file systems. By default it stays on the file system of the root.

mount_points_skipped.description: The folders on another file system that the walk counted and did not enter. 0 when cross_filesystems is true.

entries.description: The entries below the root, by kind. The root itself is not counted.

total.description: The four counts below added up.

directories.description: Folders, mount points and folders that could not be listed included.

files.description: Regular files, every name of a hard-linked file counted.

symlinks.description: Symbolic links below the root, which the walk never follows.

depth.description: The depth, counted from 1 in the order of the list.

bytes.description: The apparent size (st_size) of the regular files at this depth, every name counted.

class_key.description: The smallest value of a class of powers of two, as a string of digits: 0, 1, 2, 4, 8, and so on up to 2^63.

class_histogram.description: A histogram in classes of powers of two. The bucket 0 holds the value 0, the bucket 1 the value 1, the bucket 2 the values 2 and 3, the bucket 4 the values 4 to 7, and so on up to the bucket 2^63, which holds 2^63 and above.

count.description: How many values it counts: the sum of the bucket counts.

total.description: The values added up, stopping at the largest 64-bit number.

max.description: The largest value, 0 when there is none.

buckets.description: The smallest value of each class, as a string of digits, and how many values it holds.

class_histograms.description: Histograms by class of powers of two: the smallest value of a class, as a string of digits, and the histogram of the values that belong to it. A class that holds no value is left out.

length_histogram.description: A histogram of name lengths in bytes: one bucket for each length from 1 to 255. A longer name is counted as 255.

count.description: How many names it counts: the sum of the bucket counts.

max.description: The longest length, 0 when there is none.

buckets.description: A length as a string of digits, and how many names have it.

name_lengths.description: The lengths of names in bytes, by what the name belongs to.

hard_links.description: The regular files that have more than one name. The names of a file are one file, so they have one size and lie in one class of file_sizes, which counts every name: group_sizes_by_file_size says in which class each group lay.

groups.description: The files whose link count is above 1, each counted once however many names it has.

names.description: The names of those files that the walk found.

incomplete_groups.description: Of the groups, those whose link count is above the names found: their other names are outside the walk.

group_sizes.description: The names found per group, in classes of powers of two. A group of size 1 is a file whose other names are all outside the walk.

group_sizes_by_file_size.description: The same groups by the class of the size of their file: for each class of file size that holds a group, the names found per group in classes, as in group_sizes. A group is in the class of the size its first name had when the walk met it, and a name met with another size is not a name of the group. The histograms add up to group_sizes, and the names of a class are at most the files that file_sizes counts in that class.

symbolic_links.description: The symbolic links: how many there are, and nothing of where they point. A link is an entry of its own and the walk goes no further than the link, so whether its target exists is not asked, and the profile does not say.

directories.description: Folders that could not be opened or listed because of their permissions. Counted as folders and absent from the histograms of what a folder holds.

errors.description: Entries and folders that failed for another reason: gone before the walk reached them, on Unix a folder that was not the one inspected when the walk opened it (it changed in between; on Windows the walk cannot tell one ordinary folder from another), an input or output error, a folder deeper than 4096 levels, or a folder that is its own ancestor (a bind mount can make one), which is counted and not entered.
